Write [d]={0,...,d-1} for a natural dimension d, allowing d=0. A real core A from a left bond l to a right bond r has entries A(a,b,j), with a in [l], b in {0,1}, and j in [r]. Its flattened matrix has left-bond rows and (bit,right-bond) columns. Its fixed-bit slice is A(b). A chain C of N cores has the matrix contraction M_C(w)=A_0(w_0)...A_(N-1)(w_(N-1)); the empty chain at bond r contracts to I_r. Words are head-first: the empty word is unique and a nonempty word is a first bit paired with its tail. All initial and terminal labels are retained.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: The ambient finite instruction language also allows the single-wire bit flip X and the diagonal rotation RZ(theta)=diag(cos(theta/2)-i sin(theta/2),cos(theta/2)+i sin(theta/2)). Controlled-NOT flips its target when its control bit is one and fixes the control and other wires. A single-wire gate fixes every non-target wire, and control and target are distinct. Finite lists are chronological: later instruction matrices multiply on the left. The empty list denotes identity. Every instruction in this language is unitary, including at arbitrary exact real angles. The special-orthogonal construction below uses only RY and controlled-NOT; the general list/composition identities allow the full stated language.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: For a real determinant-one orthogonal matrix on D numeric basis labels, adjacent-row elimination gives D(D-1)/2 ordered two-level rotations, including harmless zero-angle rotations. Each pair sweep annihilates a lower entry using a signed angle that sends the two real entries to their nonnegative Euclidean length and zero; a zero pair uses angle zero. Previously fixed standard-basis columns, orthogonality, and determinant are preserved. Process columns in increasing order with bottom-up adjacent sweeps. The final remaining sign is plus because the determinant is one. Reversing the elimination list and negating its angles therefore realizes the original matrix, not its inverse.
independent_disposition_text: P08–P09 signed adjacent elimination, determinant, inverse order

source_paragraphs.exact_text: For D=2^(q+1)=2S, order the basis internally by a binary Gray enumeration: consecutive labels differ on one wire. Each adjacent two-level rotation becomes a rotation of that target wire selected by the assignment on all q other wires, fixing every basis vector outside the selected pair. If the first endpoint has target bit one rather than zero, negate the physical rotation angle to preserve the ordered two-level matrix. Transport the input matrix into Gray coordinates and transport the resulting denotation back; the external named-wire basis is unchanged.

Thus the vector on the physical bond that is one at integer label zero and zero elsewhere is exactly the all-zero input column of the empty circuit on q wires. Convert a word to a Boolean list by replacing each bit by whether it is one; this list has exactly the word length. Let rev_N(x)_i=x_(N-1-i). Reversing twice is identity, also at N=0.

Lift the earlier instruction list over the next fresh zero bit and append the newly placed stage list. source_paragraphs.exact_text: S10. Exact scope and remaining work

The gate model permits exact real RY angles and named-wire controlled-NOTs. The bound N*6*(2^q)^3 is a genuine length bound in that model. It is not a finite-bit, Clifford+T, nearest-neighbor, depth, preprocessing, or readout bound, and it does not become polynomial in another scientific input parameter merely by treating q as fixed. Nonunique factor and completion choices are not a deterministic stored-data algorithm, even though a finite instruction list exists.
independent_disposition_text: exact-real gate model and stable stronger-consumer gaps below

source_paragraphs.exact_text: Further obligations remain for a concrete sampled problem: an actual input/data producer and proof that the given cores represent its desired amplitudes with the required normalization; a deterministic refinement of factor/completion selection and angle computation with explicit storage and input-access costs; finite precision, numerical stability, rotation synthesis and accumulated error; hardware routing/depth and total resources; and any coherent oracle, inverse/control, block-encoding, accepted-branch or amplification transport. None is supplied by the instruction-count field or by a word-index bijection. This local exact-real circuit existence does not assert a new scientific algorithm or a complete preparation/block-encoding resource theorem for an externally specified function.
independent_disposition_text: exact-real gate model and stable stronger-consumer gaps below
